questions.text: Which ONE of the following statements is FALSE regarding the symbol table?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement about the symbol table:

- It tracks variable scope — true, this is one of its core jobs.
- It can be implemented using a BST — true, BSTs (or hash tables) are standard implementations.
- It is created during lexical analysis — true, entries are typically first added as identifiers are tokenized.
- "Symbol table is not required after the parsing phase" — FALSE. The symbol table is essential well beyond parsing: semantic analysis (type checking), intermediate code generation, and code optimization (e.g. register allocation) all continue to rely on it.

Answer: "Symbol table is not required after the parsing phase" is FALSE.

questions.text:
Consider the following expression: [latex] x[i]=(p+r) *-s[i]+u / w [/latex]. The following sequence shows the list of triples representing the given expression, with entries missing for triples (1), (3), and (6).
[latex] \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline (0) & + & p & r \\ \hline (1) & & & \\ \hline (2) & uminus & (1) & \\ \hline (3) & & & \\ \hline (4) & / & u & w \\ \hline (5) & + & (3) & (4) \\ \hline (6) & & & \\ \hline (7) & = & (6) & (5) \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Which one of the following options fills in the missing entries CORRECTLY?
questions.solution:
[latex]x[i]=(p+r)*(-s[i])+u/w[/latex], in evaluation order:
- (0) + p r
- (1) =[] s i [latex]\text{---}[/latex] fetch s[i]
- (2) uminus (1)
- (3) * (0) (2) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] (p+r) * ([latex]-[/latex]s[i])
- (4) / u w
- (5) + (3) (4)
- (6) []= x i [latex]\text{---}[/latex] location x[i] for storing
- (7) = (6) (5)

Answer: (1) =[] s i, (3) * (0) (2), (6) []= x i

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- An attribute grammar is an SDD whose semantic rules have no side effects [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (definition).
- "L-attributed definitions cannot always be evaluated in depth-first order" [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE. Every L-attributed definition can be evaluated by a left-to-right depth-first traversal; that is why they are called L-attributed.
- Synthesized attributes can be evaluated by a bottom-up parser during reductions [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- "All L-attributed definitions based on LR(1) grammars can be evaluated bottom-up" [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE. The marker non-terminal method is guaranteed only for L-attributed definitions on LL(1) grammars; adding markers can make an LR(1) grammar non-LR.

Answer: Options 2 and 4

questions.text:
Consider the following two sets:
[latex]\begin{array}{ll} \textbf{Set X} & \textbf{Set Y} \\ \text{P. Lexical Analyzer} & \text{1. Abstract Syntax Tree} \\ \text{Q. Syntax Analyzer} & \text{2. Token}\\ \text{R. Intermediate Code Generator } & \text{3. Parse Tree} \\ \text{S. Code Optimizer} & \text{4. Constant Folding } \end{array}[/latex]
Which one of the following options is the CORRECT match from Set X to Set Y ?
questions.solution:
Output / job of each compiler phase:
- P. Lexical Analyzer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] produces tokens (2)
- Q. Syntax Analyzer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] produces parse tree (3)
- R. Intermediate Code Generator [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] works with abstract syntax tree / IR (1)
- S. Code Optimizer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] constant folding (4)

Answer: P-2; Q-3; R-1; S-4

questions.text:
Consider the following pseudo-code.
[latex] \begin{array}{ll} L 1: & t 1=-1 \\ L 2: & t 2=0 \\ L 3: & t 3=0 \\ L 4: & t 4=4 * t 3 \\ L 5: & t 5=4 * t 2 \\ L 6: & t 6=t 5 * M \\ L 7: & t 7=t 4+t 6 \\ L 8: & t 8=a[t 7] \\ L 9: & if \; t 8 \lt = max \; goto \; L 11 \\ L 10: & t 1=t 8 \\ L 11: & t 3=t 3+1 \\ L 12: & if \; t 3 \lt M \; goto L 4 \\ L 13: & t 2=t 2+1 \\ L 14: & if \; t 2 \lt N \; goto \; L 3 \\ L 15: & max =t 1 \end{array} [/latex]
Which of of the following options CORRECTLY specifies the number of basic blocks and the number of instructions in the largest basic block, respectively?
questions.solution:
Leaders: first instruction (L1), targets of jumps (L3, L4, L11) and instructions right after a conditional jump (L10, L13, L15).

Basic blocks:
- B1: L1-L2 (2)
- B2: L3 (1)
- B3: L4-L9 (6)
- B4: L10 (1)
- B5: L11-L12 (2)
- B6: L13-L14 (2)
- B7: L15 (1)

7 basic blocks; the largest (B3) has 6 instructions.

Answer: 7 and 6
